import io, glob
q4 = glob.glob("docs/questions/q-0037.0006.0020.0001.0004-*.md")[0]
with io.open(q4, 'a', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as fh:
    fh.write("""
**Live case 2, the study run, 2026-10-24 — the door passed, the meeting failed in three places.**
The person took the offer; the same agent that had said *no* from the page ran the study, and the
study confirmed its verdict: section 3 says GoodWolf would add little here and names the pace,
a second rules file and Python as the price; the plan's seven items are ordinary PRs, GoodWolf
itself the seventh, *only if after the first six you still lose questions*. The readings and the
ledger are sound — eight disagreements met, two stalled PRs with no recorded reason, owner's
questions in six places, 53 KB of rules per session, 47 PRs a week at a 950-line median; the blind
run 14 of 14 on the four groups and 0 of 3 on contradictions, each answered from the current side
without seeing the stale copy, which the report rightly names as where the harness helps. Three
breaks: the author carried the verdict it had given before the study, and the two trial runs that
produced product-faced reports differ from this one in exactly that — their authors were fresh;
read-only was broken twice by reading agents the author sent without the rules — a stray file in
the root, a project script that ran `git fetch`; and the report was written to the host's scratch
folder, *nothing inside the repo*, the one file the shelf names never offered at the first stop.
The second stop was not asked: the agent gave its verdict and side notes. What follows: the study
is a fresh agent's, given the shelf and the tree and nothing of the conversation; the person's agent
offers, hands over and asks; whoever reads under the study carries its rules and runs nothing of the
project's; the report file is the study's one write, at the place named at the offer.
""")
q8 = glob.glob("docs/questions/q-0033.0008-*.md")[0]
with io.open(q8, 'a', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as fh:
    fh.write("""
**After the study of live case 2, 2026-10-24.** The page's verdict did not stay on the page: the
agent that gave it ran the study and the report confirmed it. The front page cannot stop a project's
own agent from judging; what the method can do is keep that judgement out of the report — the study
written by a fresh agent, the person's agent left with the offer and the question. Recorded on
q-0037.0006.0020.0001.0004; the rule is the skill's.
""")
r = "docs/rule-failures.md"
s = io.open(r, encoding='utf-8').read()
anchor = "## 62. Asked whether a project needs the harness, the agent answered from the front page — 2026-10-24"
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
entry = """## 63. The study was written by the agent that had already said no — 2026-10-24

**Rules in play:** the harness skill's *A tree that already has a method* and the shelf
`MEETING.md`: the report a product document, no comparison, no self-deprecation; the blind run a
separate fresh agent; read-only, no fetch of any kind; one file written at the place named at the
offer; the second stop one question. All read; the author of the report was the one agent the rules
never said must not write it.

**What happened.** On the rewritten front page a fresh session in xuanxue-cabinet, asked *do we
need this here?*, gave a verdict — *no, not as an install* — and offered the study with a button.
The person took it. The same agent ran the study: it read the shelf, kept the form, counted the
readings and scored the ledger honestly, and wrote a report whose section 3 says the harness would
add little here and whose plan makes the harness the seventh item of seven, after ordinary PRs. Its
own summary: *the study confirms what I said before*. Two reading agents it sent without the rules
broke read-only — a stray file in the root, a project script that ran `git fetch`. The report went
to the host's scratch folder, *nothing inside the repo*. The second stop was a verdict and side
notes, not the question.

**Why it did not fire.** The two trial runs produced product-faced reports because their authors
were fresh agents given the shelf alone. The live case gave the shelf to an agent already holding a
verdict and loyal to the project it serves; the shelf's *no comparison* governed the words and not
the conclusion. The read-only rules bound the author and not the agents it sent. The place of the
report stood in the skill's offer, which the person's agent skipped, having made an offer of its
own.

**Amendment proposed:** in the skill, the study is a fresh agent's — given the shelf and the tree
and nothing of the conversation — and the person's agent only offers, names the file, hands over,
and asks the second stop's one question; in the shelf, whoever reads under the study carries its
read-only rules verbatim and runs nothing of the project's, and the report file is the study's one
write, at the place the offer named. Landing on the user's word; graded by the next live meeting.

"""
s = s.replace(anchor, entry + anchor, 1)
io.open(r, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n').write(s)
print("recorded")
PY
git add docs/questions/ docs/rule-failures.md && printf '%s\n\n%s\n' "VERIFY: live case 2's study — the door passed, the meeting failed in three places: the author carried the verdict it gave before the study and the report confirmed it, reading agents sent without the rules broke read-only, the report written outside the tree, the second stop not asked; recorded on q-0037.0006.0020.0001.0004 and q-0033.0008, register entry 63 with the amendments proposed; the user, 2026-10-24" "Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>" > "$S/msg32.txt" && git commit -q -F "$S/msg32.txt" && git push -q origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; git log -1 --format='%h'", "description": "Check whether the other session on the front-page question touched the README, record the study's failure on both questions and in the register, commit and push"}
